terms.meaning: A reusable piece of the screen that draws part of the page, such as this viewer.
A built-in React feature that lets a component remember values, or run work, between screen updates.
A comparison of finalized projects within one industry, shown as a set of slides.
The file format used by Microsoft PowerPoint presentations.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and purpose notes
sections.what: Brings in the React library, colour and data helpers, the icons, the export helper and the five slide components. Nothing is shown to the user from this part.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer and its slides need these pieces to load data, draw the icons and build the export.
sections.watch_out: The header comment says the deck holds one slide, but the list now holds five, so that comment is out of date.

sections.name: SlideContext
sections.title: What each slide receives
sections.what: Defines the bundle of information every slide is given: the scan results, the industry name and slug, and the slide's page number out of the total.
sections.why: The comment says each slide footer must show the real page number, not a fixed number, so the page position is passed in here.

sections.name: SlideDef
sections.title: Shape of one slide entry
sections.what: Describes one slide: an internal id, the label shown in the bottom bar, and a function that draws the slide.
sections.why: Likely reason: this lets each slide be listed once and drawn only when it is shown.
sections.watch_out: The id is not used to find slides in this file, so changing it has no visible effect here.

sections.name: SLIDES
sections.title: Ordered list of slides
sections.what: Lists the five slides in order: title, cost versus schedule bubble chart, glossary, AI synthesis and reasons for failure. The order sets the page counter and the bottom bar labels.
sections.why: The comment says this is the house deck order, and that new slides are added to this list.
sections.watch_out: The export call does not pass this list, so changes here do not change the exported PowerPoint file.

sections.name: BenchmarkScanRenderer (part 1)
sections.title: Viewer state, navigation and keyboard keys
sections.what: Keeps the current slide, the debug toggle and the export status. Sets up the Export PPTX action, loads the scan data, and handles Previous, Next, Escape and the arrow keys. Builds the context for the current slide so its page number is correct.
sections.why: Likely reason: the viewer must know which slide is showing and must be able to move between them from both buttons and the keyboard.
sections.watch_out: If the data has not loaded, the export still runs, but without the chart settings, so the PowerPoint may not match the screen.

sections.name: BenchmarkScanRenderer (part 2)
sections.title: Top bar: title, export, debug and close
sections.what: Shows the Benchmark Scan title, the industry name and the project count, and buttons for Export PPTX, Debug and Close.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the actions a user needs while viewing the deck, kept in one place.
sections.watch_out: The project count comes from the list of ids passed in, not from the projects that loaded, so it still shows the full number if loading failed.

sections.name: BenchmarkScanRenderer (part 3)
sections.title: Slide area and bottom controls
sections.what: Shows the current slide inside a 16:9 frame, or a message: No projects selected, Loading scan-data, or the request error. The bottom bar has Previous, a counter with the slide label, and Next.
sections.why: Likely reason: 16:9 is the standard widescreen presentation shape, and the message tells the user why nothing is drawn.
sections.watch_out: The slide width is calculated from the window height, so a short window makes the slide small.

sections.name: BenchmarkScanRenderer (part 4)
sections.title: Debug overlay with raw data
sections.what: When Debug is on, a dark side panel covers the screen and shows the full scan data as formatted text. Clicking outside the panel closes it.
sections.why: The header comment says the raw data stays reachable for checking, so it is kept behind a toggle.
sections.watch_out: The overlay prints the whole data response as text, which can be long and slow on large scans.

summary: A full-screen slide viewer for the benchmark scan. It loads the scan data for chosen projects, shows one slide at a time with previous and next controls, exports the deck as a PowerPoint file, and offers a debug view of the raw data.
purpose: Presents the benchmark deck for the projects a user finalized, and lets the user move through the slides, save them, and inspect the raw data.
why: The header comment says the slides are kept in an ordered list so new slides can be added without changing the viewer itself.
how: 1. Receive the industry, the project ids and a close action. 2. Fetch the scan data for those projects. 3. Keep the current slide number and wire up the Escape and arrow keys. 4. Show the current slide at 16:9 with its page number and total. 5. The Export PPTX button asks the server to build the file and downloads it. 6. The Debug button shows the raw data in a side panel.
inputs: The industry slug, the list of project ids and a close callback from the parent. The scan data from fetchScanData. Keyboard keys (Escape, left arrow, right arrow) and button clicks.
outputs: The on-screen slide, a downloaded reality-scan.pptx file from the export, the raw data in the debug panel, and the close callback.
risks: Export sends the project list and the chart size to the server, which builds the file. Escape closes the viewer immediately with no confirmation. The bottom bar label and the slide list can drift apart if slides are reordered carelessly.
debug: If the viewer is empty, check that project ids were passed. If the loading or error box shows, check the scan data request and its message. If export fails, read the red message at the top of the viewer. If the PowerPoint differs from the screen, compare the chart settings built from the scan data. The Debug panel shows exactly what the viewer received.
